Creates a buffer with a specified number of channels and samples.

The contents of the buffer will initially be undefined, so use [clear()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioBuffer.html#a5f4c9ee4ad7a0f02edb709ab22bcdd61 "Clears all the samples in all channels and marks the buffer as cleared.") to set all the samples to zero.

The buffer will allocate its memory internally, and this will be released when the buffer is deleted. If the memory can't be allocated, this will throw a std::bad\_alloc exception.
